column3: “The pride” is attached to the crown in the Hebrew, rather than repeated as a description of those overcome by wine.
“That crown” identifies an unstated object; “with the hand” is not explicitly retained.
“Will take it” supplies an action; the Hebrew says he swallows it while it is still in his hand.
“At the gate” renders movement back toward the gate.
“Priests and prophets” renders singular descriptions of priest and prophet; “befuddled” replaces the image of being swallowed by wine.
“Infants” and “babies” specify the people described as weaned and removed from the breasts.
“They hear” supplies a verb before the repeated commands.
“Foreign tongues” renders a single other tongue.
“Will never be shaken” replaces “will not make haste.”
“Disturbing” renders the description of His task as foreign or alien.
